Hi everyone,

I'm Dirk, an independent researcher with a background in mechanical engineering (continuum mechanics, robotics, numerical methods). I'm fairly new to formal proof and to the Lean/Mathlib community, and I've been learning by formalizing results from two small projects of my own:

  1. Three-gap (Steinhaus) theorem — a self-contained Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization, uniform in the rotation number, with 0 sorry and standard axioms only. As far as I can tell this is the first Lean 4 formalization of the theorem (Mayero's Coq proof covers the irrational case only). Repo: github.com/dkunert/three-gap-theorem-lean
  2. Rational cut-and-project sequences — period lengths of one-dimensional rational cut-and-project sequences, with an accompanying Lean formalization (~3,700 lines, 0 sorry). Repo: github.com/dkunert/cut-and-project

I'd be glad for any pointers on community conventions, and I'm interested in whether parts of this could eventually be useful for Mathlib. I'll probably ask a more specific question over in #Is there code for X? about which pieces already exist.

Thanks, and happy to be here!
— Dirk
Thanks for the welcome, @Amlal El Mahrouss and @Stephanie Alexander!
